{{Short description|American mathematician (born 1942)}}
'''William Joseph Haboush''' (born 1942)<ref>Birth year from [https://d-nb.info/gnd/1113676876 German National Library catalog], retrieved 2024-03-21</ref> is an American mathematician, a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]].<ref>[https://math.illinois.edu/directory/profile/whaboush William Haboush], Directory, University of Illinois Department of Mathematics, retrieved 2024-03-21</ref> An [[algebraic geometry|algebraic geometer]], Haboush is the namesake of [[Haboush's theorem]], which he proved in 1975, resolving a conjecture of [[David Mumford]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Haboush | first = W. J.
 | doi = 10.2307/1970974
 | issue = 1
 | journal = [[Annals of Mathematics]]
 | mr = 382294
 | pages = 67–83
 | series = Second Series
 | title = Reductive groups are geometrically reductive
 | volume = 102
 | year = 1975
 | zbl = 0316.14016}}. See reviews by Vladimir Popov, {{MR|382294}}, "In this paper the author proves Mumford's famous conjecture on geometrically reductive groups", and by A. G. Elašvili, {{zbl|0316.14016}}, "In this paper the Mumford conjecture is proved".</ref>

Haboush completed a Ph.D. in 1969 at [[Columbia University]]. His dissertation, ''A Theory of Codimension One Phenomena with an Application to the Theory of Purely Inseparable Descent'', was jointly supervised by [[Heisuke Hironaka]] and Raymond Hoobler.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=12398}}</ref>
